 Order

The petitioner-accused is before this Court seeking grant of bail under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. in Crime No.30/2022 of D.K. Women Police Station, Puttur pending in CC No.260 of 2023 on the file of the Prl.Civil Judge and JMFC Court, Puttur, D.K. District, registered for the offences punishable under Sections 417, 376(2)(n), 509 and 506 of the Indian Penal Code (for short 'IPC'), on the basis of the first information lodged by the informant Smt. Gayatri M.
2. Heard Sri. Jagadish Baliga N., learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri. Channappa Erappa,
learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent-State.
Perused the materials on record.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner is the sole accused.
He has not committed any offences as alleged.
He has been falsely implicated in the case without any basis.

The petitioner had filed Crl.P.No.11630/2022 seeking grant of anticipatory bail and NC:
2023:KHC:29104 the same was came to be dismissed vide order dated 17.01.2023.
Thereafter, the petitioner surrendered before the investigating officer.
Now the investigation is completed and the charge sheet is filed.

In the meantime, petitioner had filed Crl.P.No.3345/2023, but later the same came to be dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 23.05.2023.
4.
Learned counsel further submits that initially the informant stated that she was in love with the petitioner and they had sexual relationship on many occasions.
She also alleged that the petitioner is threatening to throw acid on her and cause her death.
The victim is aged 28 years.
The incident is said to have taken place for the first time during September 2018 and later during March 2019.

The first information came to be lodged on 27.08.2022.
5.

Learned counsel further submitted that the statement of the victim under Section 164 of Cr.P.C was recorded on 12.09.2022 and her further statement was NC: 2023:KHC:29104 also recorded by the Investigating officer on the same day, wherein, she has stated that she had physical relationship with the petitioner only on 01.09.2018 and on 22.03.2019.
In all these statements, the victim specifically stated that the petitioner is threatening to throw acid to her and her family members.

6. Learned counsel further submitted that the petitioner had filed OS No.282/2022 on the file of learned Principal Civil Judge and JMFC, Puttur, D.K., against the victim and her father seeking permanent prohibitory injunction restraining them from compelling him to marry the victim forcefully, by lodging false complaint or by implicating in false cases.
He further submitted that the said suit came to be filed on 10.08.2022 and summons was served on victim on 25.05.2022.
Immediately, thereafter on 27.08.2022 the present complaint came to be filed.
Therefore, it is probably an after thought to compel the petitioner to marry her.

sentences.text: 2 7. Learned counsel further submitted that since the investigation is already completed, detention of the petitioner in custody would amount to pre-trial punishment.
The petitioner is the permanent resident of the address mentioned in the cause title to the petition and is ready and willing to abide by any of the conditions that would be imposed by this Court.
Hence, he prays to allow the petition.
8. Per contra, learned HCGP opposing the petition submitted that the petitioner had filed criminal petition before this court twice and both the petitions came to be dismissed.
There is threat to the life of victim and her family members, if the petitioner is enlarged on bail.
There is every possibility of he threatening or hampering the prosecution witnesses.
Hence, he prays for dismissal of this petition.

9. In view of the rival contentions urged by the learned counsel for both the parties, the point that would arise for my consideration is:
NC: 2023:KHC:29104 "Whether the petitioner is entitled for grant of bail under Section 439 of Cr.P.C.?"
10.

My answer to the above point is in 'Affirmative' for the following:
REASONS 11.
The allegation made against the petitioner by the victim is of serious in nature.
The victim is aged 28 years.
She alleges, that she was forced to have physical relationship with the petitioner and accordingly they had such relationship on 01.09.2018 and again on 22.03.2019.
It is alleged that the petitioner who promised to marry her, has refused to do so.
On the other hand, he is threatening to cause injury by throwing acid on the victim and her family members.
The investigation is completed and the charge sheet is filed.
It is not the contention of the prosecution that the petitioner is required for further investigation.
But there may be a threat on the life of the victim and her family members, if the petitioner is NC: 2023:KHC:29104 enlarged on bail.
However, the said apprehension expressed by the learned High Court Government Pleader may be taken care of by imposing stringent conditions.

Accordingly, I answer the above point in the affirmative and proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed.

The petitioner is ordered to be enlarged on bail in Crime No.30/2022 of D.K. Women Police Station, Puttur on obtaining the bond in a sum of Rs.2,00,000/- (Rupees Two Lakhs only) with two sureties for the likesum to the satisfaction of the jurisdictional Court, subject to the following conditions:
a). The petitioner shall not commit any offence against the victim or her family members.
b).
The petitioner shall not threaten or tamper with the prosecution witnesses.
